sessions.session_title: Transportation support (non-financial) – planning or coordination only (Daisy Boynton)
sessions.notes_text:
Called to check in, no answer. Sent the following text: "Hey Vantrone. Mr. Swick got back to me and said the extra $20 coming out of your paycheck is due to your arrears. He's going to look into whether there's anything he can do about reducing your license fees.

I've been researching possible transportation options. Do you have any coworkers that commute from a similar place that you do? If you can get a group of 5 of you total (make sure some of them have their license), then you can get a van through the COMET that you guys can use as your transportation to and from work for $500/month ($100 each). Maybe there's a spot you can all meet up to have the driver pick you up so your uber is much shorter?"
sessions.next_conversation_topics: Follow up on Reentry Navigation goals and Briefcase Gate 1–4 items.

sessions.session_title: Barrier removal – problem-solving or coordination support (Daisy Boynton)
sessions.notes_text: Spoke on the phone with Vantrone. This week he started getting $30 rides from the woman who lives next door to him which is saving him a lot on transportation. He wants to hold off of finding housing closer to his work in Columbia because he wants to focus on getting his license (once he gets his license his dad has a car he can drive). I let him know that RDF will open its next application cycle on Dec. 1st. He plans to pay $500 next week and the week after to get $1000 towards his license. He will send me the receipts for the RDF application.
sessions.next_conversation_topics: Follow up on Reentry Navigation goals and Briefcase Gate 1–4 items.

sessions.session_title: Barrier removal – problem-solving or coordination support (Daisy Boynton)
sessions.notes_text:
Mr. Swick got back to me about Vantrone's child support:

"For Mr. Mack, his Case ID is 3004579 with a monthly obligation of $400 and a current arrearage of $9,012.13. There are 2 children in the case and it is possible that one of them has emancipated. Mr. Mack could certainly request a modification review from the Department. But, he and the custodian did agree to a lower amount of support when the case began so it is not a “sure thing” that the support obligation would decrease. It looks like an Income Withholding Order was issued to China Jushi on 10/27/2026 so if he is employed there it should start coming out of his check shortly. I do not see any license on file so there has not been a revocation. If he does run into any issue regarding license, please let me know and we can get that figured out. Aside from that, Mr. Mack appears to be moving in the right direction with an employer on file."

I talked to Vantrone and he said China Jushi is currently taking $116 out of his paycheck weekly. He wanted Mr. Swick to confirm that was due to his arrears and not a mistake. I also asked Mr. Swick about Vantrone's suspended license to see if he could help in any way because Vantrone us currently spending $300-400 a week on ubers to and from work.
sessions.next_conversation_topics: Follow up on Reentry Navigation goals and Briefcase Gate 1–4 items.

sessions.notes_text: Vantrone asked again about help with his license. I reiterated that RDF can only pay off $750 in fees, so if he can start paying it down until he gets to $750 left, that will probably give us the best chance of an RDF approval. I also sent him the number to call Lexington DSS directly about his child support. I still haven't heard back from them over email.
sessions.next_conversation_topics: Follow up on Reentry Navigation goals and Briefcase Gate 1–4 items.

sessions.notes_text:
Vantrone completed his initial intake and consultation over the phone. He is currently residing at Timeless Transitional Housing and recently secured employment at Jushi, working 12-hour swing shifts. While he has his basic identification documents (State ID, SSN, Birth Certificate), he currently lacks a driver's license due to approximately $1,700 in unpaid fines related to seatbelt tickets. He is maintaining his sobriety and has been clean from alcohol for two years.

Despite his proactive employment efforts, Vantrone faces immediate logistical barriers. He urgently needs work clothing, as he has been wearing the same single outfit since his release on the 1st of the month. Transportation is also a significant stressor; he lives far from the bus line and relies entirely on a housemate for rides to work, causing anxiety about potential job loss. Additionally, he owes roughly $10,000 in child support arrears from his time incarcerated and has been unable to get in touch with DSS.

The navigator and Vantrone established three top priorities: Driver's License Reinstatement, Child Support Assistance, and acquiring Work Clothing. The navigator committed to researching clothing banks that align with his work schedule, contacting DSS on his behalf, and looking into the process for addressing his DMV fines. Vantrone will also attend an upcoming Vocational Rehabilitation appointment on the 28th to seek additional support.
sessions.next_conversation_topics: Follow up on Reentry Navigation goals and Briefcase Gate 1–4 items.

sessions.transcript_text:
Phone Intake/Screening: Vantrone Mack, 10/23/26

Background/Referral: Vantrone knew about Turn90 from a letter he received while in prison. He got his current job through Turn90, and Turn90 also set up a Vocational Rehab appointment for him.

Housing: He lives at Timeless Transitional Housing, 735 Wren Road, Lot 2, Lexington, SC 29073. He reports being comfortable there.

Documents:

Birth certificate: yes
SS card: yes
State ID: yes
Driver’s license: no. He needs to pay about $1,700 in fines, including about three seatbelt tickets, to reinstate it. He has been struggling to pay these alongside child support.

Transportation: This is a major barrier. He doesn’t live near a bus line. His housing provides 2 free rides per week, and he can’t afford Uber or Lyft. A friend from his housing, who was released with him, currently drives him to and from work. Vantrone is worried about losing his job if that ride falls through. He has no vehicle but says he could save for one once licensed.

Health/Behavioral Health: No prescribed medications in the last 5 years. He has no health conditions and is legally and physically able to work.

Substance Use: He has a history of major alcohol abuse, which led to homelessness. He reports 2 years sober with no alcohol in the last year, and got there on his own without a formal program. He reports no drug use other than marijuana.

Criminal History:

First arrest in his teens
About 50 total arrests, including jail. He attributes these to alcohol and to losing his mother at 15.
4–5 convictions and 4–5 incarcerations
Most recent: released from prison 10/1/26 after about 18–19 months
No drug trafficking, no firearm charges, no pending charges
Parents’ criminal history unknown

Supervision: None.

Child Support: He pays child support and is about $10,000 in arrears from his incarceration. He has tried calling DSS at the Columbia number they gave him and can’t get through.

Employment: Currently employed at Jushi USA (he spelled it J-U-S-H-I-U-S-A and calls it “Juicy”) and is happy there. He works 12-hour swing shifts, about 6:30/7 to 7, and gets only a 30-minute break.

Upcoming Days Off:

10/27, 10/28, and 10/31 (Sat)
11/2, plus a Thursday and Friday in November (dates unspecified)

Education: 9th grade

Work History: He built pontoon boats for 5 years before his most recent incarceration, which is his longest job. He has also done electrical, plumbing, and auto work.

Certifications: He previously held a forklift license and needs to renew it.

Immediate Needs: Clothing. He has been wearing the same pants and white T-shirt he was released in. His Voc Rehab appointment is Wed 10/28 at 1:00 PM, and he was told they may help with work clothes and job needs. I suggested he ask them about clothing and transportation assistance.

Program Fit: He works full-time and has transportation barriers, so I offered Reentry Navigation (phone-based support) instead of the full-time 9–3 program. He agreed.

Top 3 Goals:

Driver’s license
Child support
Clothing

Plan:

Email DSS/child support for an update on his arrears
Research clothing resources near Lexington. Catholic Charities SC has a clothing closet on Tuesdays 9:30–12, but he said that conflicts with work. Call the second clothing resource I found to ask about its hours and match them to his days off.
Research the license reinstatement process
Follow up early next week by call or text. He has saved my name and number.
